messages:
riley: Noticing a nasty interaction between the client-side rate limiter and auth retries in the new js-sdk. Paginator stops making progress and we get a flood of refreshes + duplicate page work.

sam: Can you paste the minimal repro? Which SDK and sampleapp?

riley: js-sdk@2.5, sampleapps/paginate-demo. Config: concurrency=6, windowSize=128, leakyBucketRate=200req/s. When the auth proxy injects intermittent 401s (~10% of requests in short bursts) the limiter opens a bunch of capacity spikes and the SDK's retry/backoff feeds them, causing multiple inflight retries for the same page. Result: duplicate processing + refresh storm.

maria: Hmm. We should never duplicate page processing. Are dedupe keys enabled? Paginator should mark pages in-flight.

riley: Paginator marks them, but the retry path bypasses the in-flight set while doing exponential backoff + background retry. Also token refresh is single-flight but we re-acquire the limiter tokens before re-enqueuing, so a burst of waiting callers all race to grab released tokens when limiter refills -> sudden fanout.

kai: That explains duplicates. Two things to consider: 1) make retry/resubmit paths honor the same in-flight guard (do not bypass page state), 2) treat token refresh as part of the request lifecycle so it doesn't cause reentrancy into the limiter. Prefer making retries respect the in-flight set + gentle requeueing.

sam: For parity: python-sdk and go-sdk use a queue that holds retrying task references rather than re-acquiring limiter tokens immediately; node's implementation was optimized for latency and re-acquires instantly which causes fanout. We should align node to the queue model.

maria: Agreed. Also add a limiter bucket smoothing window: when refill occurs, gradually release tokens instead of all at once (micro-bursts). Could be an opt-in config: smoothRefillMs. Default false for now.

riley: Quick mitigation I tried locally: change retry to push the failed page into a small in-memory retryQueue with jittered backoff and don't touch limiter tokens until dequeue time. That eliminated duplicates and stopped the refresh spike in my run.

kai: Good. Please put together a tiny sampleapp patch and a unit test that simulates the auth-proxy burst + asserts no duplicated page IDs processed.

riley: Will do. Pushing branch now: riley/limit-smoothing-retry-guard #1

ci-bot: CI started for branch riley/limit-smoothing-retry-guard #1

sam: Also add a runtime flag in the Paginator: { retryMode: 'queue' | 'immediate' } with default 'queue' to avoid surprising breaking changes. Document behavior in the SDK README and the SDK parity matrix.

maria: Add an observability metric: paginator.duplicates.count and auth.refresh.burst_count so we can detect this in customer signals. Also tie a small alert when duplicates > threshold.

kai: For tests: unit test ensures single-flight refresh still prevents N refresh calls, but ensure it doesn't cause limiter reentrancy. e2e should run 50 concurrent pages with auth-proxy flapping at 10% and assert progress completes and no dupes.

riley: Branch pushed + tests (unit+flaky-e2e harness). CI shows local passing. Opening PR: https://git.internal/redwood/sampleapps/pull/412 — includes retryQueue, optional smoothRefillMs, and metrics.

ci-bot: CI passed for PR riley/limit-smoothing-retry-guard #412 (unit: 23/23, e2e: 1/1) :white_check_mark:

maria: Nice. After merge, schedule a small patch release and add a KB article for customers: "App hangs or duplicate pages during auth bursts" describing pinning options and config knobs.

sam: Also update devex onboarding quickstart: include recommended Paginator defaults for high-concurrency ingestion (retryMode=queue, smoothRefillMs=250, windowMonitorMs=5000). That should reduce first-time friction.

kai: I'll draft the changelog and coordinate with eng-releases for a patch. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
